findings.claim: assert_bare_binary_shape() silently degrades to a no-op when xxd is absent. The || true fallback (intended for reliability) sets magic to empty string when xxd is not installed, causing [ "" = "1f8b" ] to be false and the gzip-shape guard to provide no protection. findings.evidence: policy-check.yml lines 252: 'magic="$(head -c 2 "${path}" 2>/dev/null | xxd -p 2>/dev/null || true)"'. If xxd is absent: xxd exits 127, stderr suppressed by 2>/dev/null, || true makes $() return empty. magic=''. Test [ '' = '1f8b' ] → false. Function returns 0. ADOPT-001 §12.7.13 'Asset-shape pin' paragraph mentions the 'defensive check' but does not note the xxd-absent degradation. Code comment says 'xxd is in vim-common, normally pre-installed but not guaranteed' — this note exists in the workflow comment context but not in ADOPT-001.
findings.impact: On GitHub-hosted ubuntu-24.04 runners, xxd IS present (vim-common in base image) — no practical impact on standard adopters. On self-hosted ubuntu-24.04 runners without vim-common, the gzip-shape guard silently no-ops. Primary control (SHA256 verify_sha256) remains intact regardless: SHA256 was computed on the known-good bare binary; a future Regal tarball would have a different SHA256 and fail at verify_sha256 before assert_bare_binary_shape is reached. Defense-in-depth gap only.
findings.mitigation: Add one sentence to ADOPT-001 §12.7.13 'Asset-shape pin' paragraph noting the silent degradation: 'On self-hosted runners without vim-common (which provides xxd), the gzip-shape guard silently no-ops; SHA256 verification (the primary control) remains effective regardless.' Alternatively: emit an explicit ::warning:: when xxd is absent rather than silently succeeding.

gzip_magic_bytes_comparison.detail: Gzip magic bytes per RFC 1952: 0x1F 0x8B. head -c 2 reads exactly those two bytes from the file. xxd -p outputs lowercase hex without separators: '1f8b' + newline. $() command substitution strips trailing newline → magic='1f8b'. Test [ "${magic}" = "1f8b" ] is correct. Comparison string matches xxd -p output exactly.
